targets.authors: Nicolaou, N., Patel, P. C., & Wolfe, M. T.
targets.title: Testosterone and tendency to engage in self-employment.
targets.evidence_quote: The aim of this study is to as closely as possible replicate the analyses carried out in Nicolaou et al. (2018) on the association between 2D:4D and self-employment; but in a new and larger sample (N more than 2100; this is more than twice the sample size used in Nicolaou et al., 2018).
targets.outcome_quote: Here, we find no substantive evidence of an association between 2D:4D and self-employment, contradicting the conclusions for left-hand 2D:4D in Nicolaou et al. (2018).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly contradict the original left-hand finding; their overall central verdict is failure despite agreement on the right-hand null.

targets.authors: Bönte, W., Procher, V. D., & Urbig, D.
targets.title: Biology and selection into entrepreneurship: The relevance of prenatal testosterone exposure.
targets.evidence_quote: In an additional not preregistered exploratory analysis, we test for an association between 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent in our data using a measure of entrepreneurial intent similar to one of the measures used by Bönte et al. (2016).
targets.outcome_quote: In an additional not preregistered exploratory analysis, we test for an association between 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent in our data using a measure of entrepreneurial intent similar to one of the measures used by Bönte et al. (2016). We find no statistically significant or suggestive evidence of an association between 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent in this analysis.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Exploratory new-sample retest of the reported digit-ratio/entrepreneurial-intent association; original significant negative association is described in the introduction, while this corresponding analysis finds none.

reasoning: Primary new-sample replication plus an exploratory retest of a second published association. Original-data pooled estimation for meta-analysis is ancillary to the central new-sample replication. Full-text title, authors and DOI match the assignment.
